page.layout: One printed page (page 126). Running head at top, page number at left of it. Main text: the end of a verse poem, then a centred rule, a centred title with subtitle, and a verse poem below. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Addo, cur tumeant audaci pectora fastu, Quum tenuis fumus, pulvis & umbra fiem? Vrget propositum rigidus subigitque rebellem, Pressus sæpe manus cogor & arma dare. Quid faciam? quo me subnixus vindice tuter? Quis certum imbelli iam ferat auxilium? Sed mihi, serpentis qui vafri, Christe, dolosas Artes vicisti, solus adesse velis. Nam si consilium virésque in prælia mittas, Vincetur subito qui modo victor erat.
main_text.head: IN LIBRVM IOANNIS De Leri, quo Americæ historiam descripsit.
main_text.p: IGnotas quondam, & nostro procul orbe remotas Gentes, monstrosa barbarieque feras, Stridentesque sonos linguæ, ventresque nefandos Humanis saturos carnibus ecce refers. Credo, equidem, Lerae, doces nam visa: sed euge Te dignum nodum vindice solve precor. Talia, dic, portenta hominum tam rara benigni Temperies cæli num generare queat: Et quos inculta mites creat arbore fructus Mite solum, indomita fertilitate nitens? Ꝑ. Horrida monstra hominum quaris num gignat amæna Temperies cæli, fertilitásque soli?

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "fiem" (line 2 of first poem; possibly "fiam" or "siem"), "quaris" (possibly "quaeris"), "subnixus" (print reads "fubnixus"), "Ꝑ." (the leading mark before "Horrida" is uncertain; it may be a reference or sign). The initial "I" is a large woodcut initial joined to "Gnotas". Right-hand edge shows faint show-through from the facing page, not transcribed.
